passages.t: ‘Praise the LORD, all you nations’: the shortest psalm
passages.happening:
Psalm 117 is the shortest psalm in the Bible. It has only two verses.

The first is a call. “Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol Him, all you peoples!” (verse 1). To extol is to praise highly.

The second gives the reason. “For great is His loving devotion toward us, and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Hallelujah!” (verse 2).
passages.hearers:
A hymn of praise usually has two parts: a call to praise, and the reason, often starting with ‘for’. Psalm 117 is that shape and nothing more. It is a hymn with everything extra taken away.

What would surprise a first hearer is who is called. Not Israel only, but ‘all you nations’ and ‘all you peoples’. In the ancient world each nation usually worshipped its own gods. Here every people on earth is invited to praise Israel's God.

And look at the reason. The nations are to praise God for his loving devotion ‘toward us’, that is, toward Israel. God's faithful love for one people shows the whole world what kind of God he is. When he keeps his promises to Israel, that is good news for everyone. God told Abraham at the very start, “all the families of the earth will be blessed through you” (Genesis 12:3).

‘Loving devotion’ is the Hebrew word hesed, God's loyal love that keeps its promises. The book page explains it. This psalm is part of the Hallel, as the note on Psalm 113 explains.
passages.later:
Paul quotes verse 1 in his letter to the Romans: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples” (Romans 15:11). He sets it beside other Old Testament lines to show that God always meant to bring the nations to praise him through Christ (Romans 15:8-11). ‘Gentiles’ means the nations who are not Jewish.

Isaiah promised that God's house would be “a house of prayer for all the nations” (Isaiah 56:7). And John saw “a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue” standing before God's throne (Revelation 7:9).
passages.asks:
Psalm 117 is short enough to learn by heart in a minute. Try it.

It also asks how large your picture of God's people is. The call goes to every nation. No people on earth is left out of it, and no people is above it.
